summary: A completed source/interface pass for the audited process layer SF.6: nine coefficient- and hypothesis-specific consumer contracts account for crystalline/prismatic, analytic, l-adic and cycle/trace handoffs. There are no SF.6 mathematical declarations, APIs, definition unit tests or planets. The packet retains exact supplier frontiers, seven ownership requests and seven gaps. It proposes retiring the process bridge and routing comparisons directly to mathematical consumers, while applying no structural change or upward foundation prerequisite.

contracts.title: Native sites, coefficients and foundation boundary
carriers: An abelian sheaf F on a named Grothendieck site (C,J), with HasSheafify and HasExt; H^q(F) is Ext from the constant integral sheaf.
The native small pro-étale site X.ProEt and ProEt.topology X; its coefficient ellAdicSheaf is obtained from continuous maps into the topological group Z_l.
Br′(X) is the torsion subgroup of H²_et(X,G_m); it is distinct from the Azumaya Brauer group unless a comparison theorem applies.
hypotheses: X is a scheme; l is prime for the native l-adic coefficient sheaf.
The native cohomology definition imposes no invertibility condition on l. Smooth base change, purity and the comparison contracts below have additional hypotheses.
contracts.map: Reuse CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H, Sheaf.H.map and Scheme.EllAdicCohomology. H.map changes a sheaf on one fixed site; it is not a morphism-of-sites comparison. The inequality etaleTopology ≤ proetaleTopology concerns the big scheme topologies and is not a cohomology isomorphism.
compatibility: Preserve the small/big-site equivalence and universe lift rather than defining a private cohomology type.
Use the inherited equivariant-sheaf carrier and its invariant-section spectral sequence for real descent, not the ordinary cohomology of the fixed locus.

Do not identify the topological Z_l coefficient sheaf with the discrete constant sheaf by definitional equality.

carriers: A smooth proper scheme X over C; algebraic de Rham hypercohomology of Omega^bullet_(X/C).

For a characteristic-zero field k and embedding sigma:k→C, apply the comparison to X_sigma; identification with H_dR(X/k)⊗_(k,sigma)C is a separate scalar-base-change map.
hypotheses: q≥0; X/C smooth and proper for the supplier node.
Families, nonproper/logarithmic curves, arbitrary connections and singular bases require their own C5 statements.
contracts.map: The algebraic-to-holomorphic de Rham hypercohomology map, followed by analytic Poincaré and sheaf-to-singular comparison, gives c_DB:H^q_dR(X/C)→H^q_sing(X^an,C). Proper GAGA and analytic Poincaré make this named map an isomorphism; a chosen equivalence of equal-dimensional spaces does not qualify.
compatibility: Require c_DB,Y ∘ f* = f_an* ∘ c_DB,X for morphisms f:Y→X in the admitted class.
Require c_DB(x cup y)=c_DB(x) cup c_DB(y), retaining degrees and the cochain-product comparison.

A trace diagram must name the Tate period/orientation normalization. With the usual integration convention the expected untwisted divisor factor is 2πi, not 1; this strengthened statement is a C5 request, not an export of the additive repair node.

acceptance: For Spec C, degree zero sends 1 to 1; positive degrees vanish.
For P¹, compare the actual divisor/trace generators with the chosen period normalization; equality of dimensions in degrees 0 and 2 is insufficient.
Transport along each specified embedding sigma, not an unspecified complex realization.

contracts.title: Finite-coefficient étale–Betti and local-system interface
carriers: A finite-type C-scheme X, its small étale topos, and the classical analytic topology on X(C).
A finite locally constant abelian coefficient sheaf, or the constructible torsion sheaves admitted by the relative theorem.
hypotheses: For relative f:X→S, X and S are locally of finite type over C and f is of finite type; F is abelian torsion.
SGA 4 XVI 4.1 requires f proper or F constructible for comparison of all R^q f_*; the finite locally constant absolute case uses the constructible alternative.
This torsion statement is not a theorem for arbitrary nonconstructible Q_l sheaves.
contracts.map: The inverse-image comparison epsilon* R^q f_et,* F→R^q f_an,* epsilon*F is an isomorphism in this range. For S=Spec C it gives H^q_et(X,F)→H^q(X(C),F_an); for finite local systems use the sheaf/singular bridge with those coefficients.
compatibility: Require naturality in F and f and compatibility with exact coefficient sequences and their connecting maps.
Identify mu_n with the chosen Tate coefficient line; do not erase it when comparing divisor classes.
The rational Betti/l-adic map after an embedding uses S6, not tensoring the torsion theorem without a limit argument.

carriers: Complex smooth X and n>0: H²(X(C),Z/n(1)), retaining a choice if the twist is written as Z/n.
Real smooth integral X; G=Gal(C/R), the sign G-module Z/n(1), and equivariant Betti cohomology H^q_G(X(C),−).
The cohomological Brauer group Br′ and the Picard group, independently of an Azumaya comparison.
hypotheses: Use R=the real numbers for ordinary Betti topology; general real closed fields use the semi-algebraic site, not an unprovided analytic manifold.
For the degree-one units formula require X/R proper and geometrically connected, so Gamma(X,O_X)^×=R^×.
Use the finite Kummer sequence on the étale site, where n is invertible in these characteristic-zero cases.

compatibility: Construct the real comparison using equivariant descent and the same coefficient action; do not replace H_G by H(X(R),−).
Require the connecting maps and reduction maps in n to commute with comparison.
The compatibility with intersection/cycle products belongs to S9 and MC.2; it is not a prerequisite of this Kummer prefix.

contracts.title: Derived l-adic limit and rational realization boundary
carriers: A compatible tower of finite coefficients Lambda_n=Z/l^n or a specified finite-free lisse integral lattice with its derived reductions.
R lim_n RΓ_et(X,Lambda_n), with its Galois action when X descends to a field k.
The native pro-étale Z_l coefficient cohomology and the rational realization obtained after scalar extension to Q_l.
hypotheses: Identify the derived coefficient object with R lim of its derived reductions using a stated derived-completeness theorem.
To replace H^q R lim by lim H^q, require lim¹ H^(q−1)=0, e.g. a Mittag–Leffler tower; finite finite-level groups give that property.
For H_B(X(C),Q)⊗Q_l≅H_et(X_kbar,Q_l), use a specified embedding kbar→C, finite-generation/finite-complex inputs and a compatible integral comparison.

For the Ichino–Prasanna use, work at a sufficiently small level on its smooth compact Shimura variety, with the number-field representation rho factoring through G/Z_s; the associated local system and a compatible integral lattice must be supplied by the Shimura/local-system owner.
contracts.map: Retain 0→lim¹ H^(q−1)(K_n)→H^q(R lim K_n)→lim H^q(K_n)→0 before taking an ordinary limit. Compose the finite comparison maps with the derived limit map, identify the actual native sheaf cohomology, then invert l. Transport the G_k action along the resulting comparison; no pre-existing G_k action on an arbitrary Betti space is assumed.
compatibility: Reduction, cup products and pullback must commute at every level and with the derived-limit identifications.
The continuous G_k representation and a chosen Betti comparison depend on the chosen embedding; a source cannot claim embedding independence from dimension equality.
Tensoring with Q_l removes integral torsion and therefore cannot certify an integral comparison or lattice recovery.

At a fixed level K, finite étale correspondence pullback/transfer gives Hecke equivariance of Equation (2.1); passage over levels uses the compatible transition maps. Finite-coefficient comparison on a constant sheaf alone does not supply the representation-valued local system.
